memo.verdict: Bullish on direction; progress to Early-Stage Assessment; conviction a working hypothesis (medium-low). The park rule does not fire: management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) C, business quality (E 2, BB 2) C, predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) C, trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) C, so no D or F on the four gates. Preferred entry SEK 230 or below, where the modal path returns about 28% a year over eighteen months and the adverse drop-through about 15%. At SEK 247.8 (22 Sep 2026) the case clears the 20% bar with almost no margin (the bar clears below SEK 252 on the modal path; below SEK 219 on the adverse drop-through). At SEK 247.8 a first position would be built only on the Q3 2026 report (23 Oct 2026) showing core organic growth at 5% or more with the transport backlog cleared, the Water & Bioeconomy margin at or above 21.8%, and at least one further acquisition disclosed at 9x or less. The case is "a bet on the odds, not a bet with a floor"; the downside is the cohort multiple, SEK 165 to SEK 211 on 24-month-forward EPS of SEK 18.35.
case: - Thesis: Sdiptech is a repaired serial acquirer, not yet a compounder; a new chief executive has sold what hid the core's 21% margins and 11% organic growth, and at SEK 247.8 the shares pay for the repair but not for the 15% return on capital the re-rating needs. On about 15% a year modal earnings growth and no dividend the return clears the 20% bar over eighteen months at a blended multiple, only just, and only because the record gives even odds or a little better to the market moving the stock out of its low-quality cohort.

- The change is internal, multi-dimensional and dated, made by the company rather than done for it: chief executive 1 Jun 2025 with a returning chief financial officer; review Jul 2025; eleven service-heavy units plus Metus sold by Q2 2026 at 6.7x for SEK 295m; SEK 184m preference shares redeemed; SEK 250m bonds repurchased; ROCE target above 15% set and put into pay; acquisitions restarted Apr 2026. Five of twelve internal forces strong (chief executive A, perimeter reduction A, strategy change A, other leaders B, standards improvement B; also balance sheet B, acquisitions B); none of seven red flags fires (dangerous leverage borderline at 2.80x against 3.0x). External forces net to a small tailwind in the growth segments (37% of 2025 EBITA) and a headwind in the largest currency (49% of core sales UK, hedged twelve months); macro D, demand B, own cycle B, political and regulatory B, competition C, supply C, disruption C.

- The change has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain: people, choices, actions, key operating metrics (organic +11%, cash conversion 90% LTM, ROCE 13.2%), financial statements (core adjusted EBITA SEK 988m LTM at 21.2%), sell-side estimates (FY2027 mean +7.8% over six months). 'Financial Outputs' B: all four key metrics improved (B each); the margin rise is mix from divestment (like-for-like core margin -0.6 points; gross margin 59.3% from 61.1%), the underlying margin flat; reported group lines lag because consensus FY2026 revenue falls 3.6% on divestments. Sell-side upgrades B (FY2026 mean +7.9% one month, +3.6% three months; targets from about SEK 290 in February 2026 to SEK 340 and SEK 325; not A because twelve-month revision -10.7% and two-broker coverage). Goldilocks growth B at all horizons; the FY2026 +94.6% consensus growth is a basis effect from a SEK 7.22 base carrying the impairment and discontinued operations, not extrapolated. Staircase C: dated steps (Q3 on 23 Oct 2026; acquisitions; FY2026 report Feb 2027 as first clean product-only year; ROCE toward 15% through 2027; 2030 ambition) but none novel; possible novel step a larger platform acquisition in Germany, undated.
counter_case: - At its strongest: Sdiptech is a Tier 6 serial acquirer that has cleaned its portfolio but not its model. It buys small businesses at 7x to 9x EBITA for initial yields of 11% to 14%, funds them with variable-rate debt and earn-outs, and earns a spread of a few points over its cost of capital that goodwill and amortisation turn into a 13% return on capital; it has never earned 15%, and the two largest areas' returns fell in the last quarter (Supply Chain & Transportation -4 points, Water & Bioeconomy -18 points). Half its sales are in a currency it hedges twelve months at a time without a disclosed ratio. The Q2 2026 organic growth of 11% was backlog clearance in transport; the 70% cash conversion followed a quarter at 54% and a quarter at 134% and reflects inventory timing. The earn-out liabilities of about SEK 900m are deferred debt that the accounting lets the company write back through profit when acquired units miss, so the reported recovery can be a false friend. The sell-side is two houses at 100% buy: crowding, not confirmation. The market has shown in Storskogen and Volati what it pays for this model when the growth stops: 9x. Fair value on that view is the cohort's 9x to 11.5x on about SEK 18 of 24-month-forward EPS, SEK 165 to SEK 211; the shares at SEK 247.8 are 15% to 33% above fair.

- The bundle version (BB 4): the case is a collection of tolerable weaknesses fatal in combination, and the framework's own count says so: seven attributes at D, two red-flag patterns forming, three shock sub-types present, 33 units, no internal audit, a twelve-month hedge, earn-outs due, a leverage ceiling within SEK 250m of EBITDA-multiple room. In the dual shock (a UK recession with a weaker pound) the hedges roll off, the fixed-price contracts block pass-through, the earn-outs consume the cash, leverage stops the engine, and a decentralised group without an internal audit sees it late. On that reading the case should be parked whatever the multiple.
triggers: - Q3 2026 report, 23 Oct 2026: core organic growth at 5% or more with the transport backlog cleared; Water & Bioeconomy margin at or above 21.8%; at least one further acquisition disclosed at 9x or less. These are the conditions for a first position at SEK 247.8.

- Cleared-branch condition (dated to the FY2027 report): FY2027 adjusted EPS at or above SEK 16.5 with group ROCE at 14% or above. Invalidate on the re-rating driver: the condition failed at the FY2027 report.

- Organic growth: alarm below 5% core organic at the Q3 2026 report; invalidate on two consecutive quarters below 3% core organic, or Supply Chain & Transportation growth at zero once the backlog is cleared.

- Acquisition engine: alarm if no third acquisition by the FY2026 report in February 2027; invalidate on a deal disclosed above 10x EBITA, or leverage back above 3.0x to fund one; alarm on any deal above 9x; modal case SEK 75m or more of acquired EBITA a year at 9x or less.

- Return on capital: alarm if the largest segment's ROCE falls again at the FY2026 report; invalidate on group ROCE below 14% at the FY2027 report with the largest segment's ROCE still falling; modal 14% or better at the FY2027 report on the way to 15%.

- Pound and UK demand: invalidate on GBP/SEK 10% weaker with the Water & Bioeconomy margin still below 22%; monitor GBP/SEK daily, UK manufacturing and construction PMIs monthly, UK living-wage announcements, any hedge-ratio disclosure.

judgement.title: APM PMS Q&A SOP: the session run on Monday 26 October 2026 on Friday 23 October's closing prices, for your session on Tuesday 27 October
judgement.heading: Sdiptech | Middle Innings Core Investment, no sell signal | 5.05% of the fund's capital in 3 tranches
judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** Sdiptech is in Industrials and capital goods. Industrials and capital goods' Industry RS was 46 at the Friday 23 October reading (73 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** Sdiptech is in Diversified industrial groups. That sector's Sector RS was 89 at the 30 September month-end (61 at the August month-end)
  - Sdiptech's sector's other companies, with their daily Stock RS, all in the Pool of Stocks Eligible for Middle Innings Portfolio Selection: thyssenkrupp (89), Aalberts (81), Hill & Smith (69), Schouw & Co (93), TKH Group (85), Indus Holding (94), and 9 more
- **Cohort:** Sdiptech is in Diversified serial acquirers in a reset. The cohort's relative strength was 83 on Friday's daily reading (78 four weeks earlier). Sdiptech's cohort's other companies: Indus Holding (94), Storskogen (59), Volati (0)
- **Sdiptech's charts are on Sdiptech's page on the PMS Per-stock Dashboard:** https://vfhqi.github.io/ratings/pms/holding.html?t=SDIP.B-SE

**What is going on, and why it matters**
- **The price move, by beta:** over twenty sessions Sdiptech's shares rose about 9%; Sdiptech's beta of 1.36 implies a small fall, so Sdiptech's own move was about +9%, 1.2 times its usual size; Sdiptech closed Friday about 3% below its 52-week high
  - Sdiptech rose 4.6% on Friday 23 October, the day the 16 October note expected Sdiptech's third-quarter results; I could not find the report itself, so I cannot say what the market read in it
- **The sector:** diversified industrial groups still lead Industrials and capital goods, while Industrials and capital goods as a whole fell sharply this week, so Sdiptech is holding up inside a weakening industry
- **The analysts:** for Sdiptech, Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates was +67% and Net Upgrade Breadth, target prices +50% at the 30 September month-end; Sdiptech's Sell-side Momentum rating eased from A to B this week

**What it means for the position**
- **Holding:** hold Sdiptech; no Sell Criterion is met, and Sdiptech passes every test of the Pool of Stocks Eligible for Middle Innings Portfolio Selection
- **Selling:** Sdiptech's nearest trigger is the relative 52W high trigger at about SEK 202.6, about 23% below Friday's close of SEK 264.00; a Sdiptech sale is unlikely this quarter
- **Adding:** no add this week; Sdiptech is about 4% above its rising 50-day moving average (SEK 252.7), so your retest test is not met, and I have not seen the third-quarter numbers the memo's add depends on

**What we could lose:** about 1.17% of the fund's capital, if Sdiptech's price falls to its relative 52W high trigger, the largest single amount among the holdings with no sell signal

**Experiment: which stocks Sdiptech's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)
- **Attendo** (same country of listing): 0.30 and 0.29, weak
- **Munters** (same country of listing): 0.27 and 0.21, weak
- **HMS Networks** (same country of listing): 0.28 and 0.13, weak
- **Bravida** (same country of listing): 0.25 and 0.18, weak
- **My reading:** Sdiptech's moves are mostly its own

**The Investment Analyst's memo on Sdiptech (1 October, at SEK 247.80; digest of 22 September)**
- **Decided:** the memo on Sdiptech is bullish on direction and progresses the case, with medium-low conviction; the quality gate does not bite (management C, business quality C)
- **Must happen:** at the third-quarter results, core organic growth of 5% or more with the transport backlog cleared, a Water and Bioeconomy margin of 21.8% or more, and one more acquisition at 9 times profit or less
- **Main risk:** Sdiptech is a serial acquirer that has cleaned its portfolio but not its model, earning a thin spread over its cost of capital
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** clears our bar of 20% a year below about SEK 252, about 5% below Friday's close; the memo's preferred entry is SEK 230 or below
- **Next test:** the third-quarter results against the memo's three tests, which the Investment Analyst has not yet read

**My judgement:** bullish on holding Sdiptech, medium conviction
- Sdiptech is the strongest holding on the rule's readings and held up while its industry fell; an add waits for the third-quarter numbers to be read against the memo
- **Counter-case:** Sdiptech is near its 52-week high with the memo's bar crossed by the price, and the largest amount we could lose among the holdings with no sell signal sits in Sdiptech

**What would change my view:** the third-quarter results against the memo's three tests; a pullback to the rising 50-day moving average with those tests met would be the add
